results.summary_before: This design implements a stochastic-computing multiplier, adder, and self-multiplier that operate on serial bitstreams. Two 9-bit repeating input streams enter on ui[0] and ui[1], and the multiplier, adder, and self-multiplier results appear as serial outputs on uo[0], uo[1], and uo[2], with uo[3] resetting the clock counter; the self-multiplier uses only the first stream. Testing involves feeding the repeating streams and reading the resulting 9-bit serial outputs. The documentation consists mainly of images with little explanatory text, and an ADALM2000 is listed as external hardware.

results.summary_before: Wirecube is a VGA demo that renders a rotating 3D wireframe cube, submitted for the Tiny Tapeout demoscene competition. It uses an optimized edge function to draw lines by evaluating magnitude thresholds, and stores cube vertices in a ROM to efficiently generate the wireframe. The design outputs VGA signals through a Tiny VGA Pmod and operates at a clock frequency of 50.35 MHz; input pins control background color, cube color, and animation speed. Silicon testing confirmed that the cube rotates and displays effects, though occasionally it stops rotating and turns into a sole rectangle.
